ci(mutation): mutate a landing twice, not three times, and stop each run at its first failure (#98)

Mutation testing took 240 of 488 CI job minutes over 2026-11-05..07 (817
runs), and ran three times per landed PR, once for a reader that does
not exist. This keeps the two runs something acts on, makes each
mutant's test run stop at its first failure, and fixes `devRed`, which
the remaining post-merge run depends on.

## Before / After

| Mutation run | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| PR (`pull_request`) | runs; the Land gate requires it green | runs,
with `--bail` |
| Merge queue (`merge_group`) | runs; nothing reads it, the queue lands
on `validate` alone | skipped |
| Push to `dev` | runs; read by `devRed`, but `devRed` usually read the
Merge bot's green push run instead | runs, with `--bail`; `devRed` reads
CI's push runs only |

```ts
// scripts/land-loop/merge-bot/main.ts
`repos/${repo}/actions/workflows/ci.yml/runs?branch=dev&event=push&status=completed&per_page=1`
```
The old query took the latest completed push run of any workflow.
`merge-bot.yml` also runs on push, ends in ~13 s and is green; the API
listed it first on each of the last three pushes (43e27e7, 632fed5,
bcdbaab), so a red `validate` or `mutation` on `dev` could not hold
landings.

## Decisions

- **Drop the queue run, keep the push run** rather than drop the push
run: the queue's result is read by nothing (Merge bot reads PR-head
checks, `repost.ts` re-posts only `agent-review` and `land-gate`, the
ruleset does not require `mutation`). The ruleset refuses
non-fast-forward pushes to `dev`, so each push's `before` is an ancestor
and every PR of a queue group falls in one push's range. Undo: revert
the `if:` in `ci.yml`.
- **Keep `scripts/ci/mutation.ts`** rather than an off-the-shelf tool:
StrykerJS's incremental mode, with the command runner `bun test` needs,
sees no test changes and would hide the weakened-tests check; no tool
found does the base comparison.
- **No scheduled full run**: each PR that touches a module already
mutates it whole with a fixed seed, so a weekly run would repeat the
same survivors.

## Checks

- `tier: human` — no `.claude/github-flow.json` in this repository.
- `/code-review` (high) of the branch: 3 findings. Fixed: a header
comment line past the print width. Kept: `snapshotOf`'s use of
`devCiRunsPathOf` is tested through the path builder only, as
`ciRunsPathsOf` is. Left open below: `devRed` lag.
- `bun check`: 474 tests, 0 fail, coverage floor passes.
- New `devRed` query called on GitHub: returns `CI success 43e27e7`.
- `bun scripts/ci/mutation.ts run --base HEAD~1` on a throwaway change
to `app/src/commands/count.ts`: 4 mutants tested, 0 undetected, `--bail`
in the command.
- `--bail` on `decide.ts` against `decide.test.ts`, 4 runners, 16-core
machine, 3 runs per mode: without 371 s (load 16), 280 s, 264 s (load
1-6); with 212 s (load 16), 174 s, 182 s (load 6-8). Medians 280 s / 182
s, -35 %. Same 21 survivors every run by line, column, mutator and
replacement.

| Test | Mutant | Seen failing |
|---|---|---|
| `dev is red by the latest push run of CI alone, never another
workflow's` | the old any-workflow path | unknown |
| `ci.yml's mutation job skips the merge queue, …` | the `if:` removed |
unknown |

## Left open

- `devRed` reads the latest *completed* CI push run: while a push's
mutation runs (up to ~19 min), landings go on reading the previous run.
Pre-existing.
- `--bail`'s gain in CI is not measured: this PR touches no listed
module, so its own `mutation` job exits in seconds. The first later PR
touching `decide.ts` measures it against job 128544857250 (head pass 658
s, base pass 279 s).
- The cut from 3 to 2 runs per landed PR is measured after landing, by
counting mutation runs per landed PR.

fix(merge-bot): key the CI-push Sweep on `sweep`, and test which PRs a start serves

Answers the agent review of PR #98. The CI-push Sweep took the concurrency
group of `workflow_run.pull_requests[0]`, which GitHub fills with any open PR
whose head is `dev` (a dev -> main release PR): it could run beside another
Sweep and race on that PR's state record. A push `workflow_run` now keys on
`sweep` first. The choice between the named PR, a completed run's commit PRs
and every open PR moves into `startOf`, a pure function with its own test;
main.ts's header lists RUN_EVENT, and AGENTS.md names the CI-push Sweep.

docs(ci): say the push mutation run detects, not prevents, what landed together

Answers the agent review's nit on PR #98: the comment read as if the post-landing
run replaced the queue's check; it catches a combination of PRs after landing
and holds every landing through devRed.

fix(merge-bot): sweep when CI completes on a push to dev

`devRed` reads CI's latest completed push run on dev, but the push's own
Sweep starts while that run is in progress and reads the previous one. CI's
completion on a push was filtered out (`workflow_run.event == 'pull_request'`),
so a red dev was seen only at the next cron Sweep, up to 30 minutes later,
and a green-again dev released held PRs only then. CI's push completion now
starts a Sweep: `RUN_EVENT` tells the Merge bot to read every open PR, since
the PR the commit landed is closed. Found by the agent review of PR #98.

ci(mutation): stop each mutant's test run at its first failing test

Stryker's command runner reads only the exit code, so the tests after the
first failure add time and nothing to the verdict. On decide.ts with
decide.test.ts, 4 test runners, a 16-core machine, three runs per mode:
without `--bail` 371 s (load 16), 280 s and 264 s (load 1-6); with it 212 s
(load 16), 174 s and 182 s (load 6-8). Medians 280 s and 182 s, -35 %. The
same 21 survivors each time, by line, column, mutator and replacement. A
test that fails before a timeout turns a Timeout into Killed; both count as
detected, and the base and head passes both bail.

ci(mutation): stop mutating in the merge queue, which nothing reads

The ruleset requires `validate`, not `mutation`, so the queue lands a group
on `validate` alone and the queue's mutation run ends after the merge. No
reader looks at it: the Merge bot reads the PR head's checks, `repost.ts`
re-posts only `agent-review` and `land-gate`, and `devRed` reads push runs.
Over 2026-11-05..07 it cost 46 job minutes across 14 runs.

Two runs stay: the PR's, which the Land gate requires green, and the push
to dev's, measured from `before`, which `devRed` reads. The ruleset refuses
non-fast-forward pushes to dev, so `before` is an ancestor and every PR of a
queue group falls in one push's range.

The push skip (`testedAlready`) waited for the queue's green check and goes,
with the token and `checks: read` it needed and the merge-queue base.

fix(merge-bot): read dev's red from CI's push runs alone

`devRed` read the latest completed push run on dev of any workflow. The
Merge bot's own push run starts in the same second as CI's, ends in about
13 s and is green, so the API listed it first on each of the last three
pushes (43e27e7, 632fed5, bcdbaab): a red `validate` or `mutation` on dev
could not hold the landings. The query now names `ci.yml`.

fix(land-loop): ask the Routing judge only about the judged paths a Patch delta touches (#91)

## What changed

On a Patch delta, the Routing judge reads only the delta's diff. But for
a mixed (`ruled-then-judged`) PR, `judgeAskOf` asked it about the judged
paths of the whole PR. If the delta left those paths alone, the judge
got an empty diff and sent the PR to the Owner. That is what happened on
PR #88: its round-1 fix touched only a factory path, while `.gitignore`
was its judged path.

All changes to `scripts/land-loop/routing/routing-rules.ts`; `main.ts`
is unchanged:

- **`judgeAskOf`**: on a mixed PR, it now asks about the judged paths
that the delta's own rules still judge.
  - Delta `ruled` (every path it touches is ruled): asks nothing.
- Delta `ruled-then-judged`: asks about the judged paths the PR and the
delta share, and nothing when they share none.
- Delta `judged` (no rule names its paths): asks about the PR's judged
paths, as before. Every path in the delta is judged, so git's pathspec
already limits the diff to the paths the delta touches.
  - No Patch delta: asks about the PR's judged paths, as before.
- **`routingOf`**: it takes from `judgeAskOf` whether the judge was
asked, so the two cannot drift.
  - A mixed PR whose delta asks nothing keeps the rules' answer.
  - A mixed PR that was asked but has no judge answer still throws.

In `main.test.ts`, the git fixture setup moves into `fixtureRepo`. The
moved-file test and the new Patch delta test both use it.

Closes #89

## How I verified it

- `routing-rules.test.ts`:
- PR #88's shape under the lab's policy asks the judge nothing and keeps
`auto` with a deep review.
  - A delta that touches `.gitignore` still asks about `.gitignore`.
  - Partial and zero overlap of judged paths each have a test.
- The `judged`-delta and the `ruled`-delta cases have tests, and so does
a ruled PR whose delta the judge sends to the Owner.
  - The throws when the judge is missing still hold.
- `main.test.ts`: a fixture-repo test runs through base, the reviewed
head, then two later heads.
  - A delta that touches only `scripts/a.ts` asks nothing.
- A delta that touches `.gitignore` asks about `.gitignore`. The judge's
diff (`judgeDiffArgs`) is not empty and leaves `scripts/a.ts` out.
- `bun check` passes: 475 tests, 0 fail.
- `bun scripts/ci/mutation.ts run` on `routing-rules.ts`: 0 mutants
survive on the changed lines. The first run left one: a judge's `owner`
answer on a ruled PR's delta could change its route. A new test now
covers it.
- `guarantees.test.ts` passes without a change: it already passes a
judge answer only when `judgeAskOf` asks.

## Out of scope

A `judged` PR whose Patch delta is empty still asks the judge over an
empty diff. It is recorded as a separate finding, outside #89's
acceptance criteria.

fix(land-loop): give the Author a marked way to comment on its PR (#88)

## What changed

An Author that explained its decisions with `gh pr comment` posted an
unmarked comment, so its PR watch woke it on its own words (PR #86). The
Owner and the Author post under one gh login, so only `AUTHOR_MARK`
tells them apart. Until now, only `thread.ts` added the mark, and only
for review-thread replies.

- **`scripts/land-loop/comment.ts`** (new): `bun
scripts/land-loop/comment.ts <pr> "<comment>"` posts a conversation
comment that ends with `AUTHOR_MARK`, the same way `thread.ts` marks a
thread reply. A missing PR number, a non-integer one or a blank comment
prints the usage line.
- **Stop hook message** (`stop/decide.ts` `armReason`, `stop/hook.ts`):
the message that tells the Author to arm its PR watch now names
`comment.ts` with the PR number. It says to use it to explain a
decision, never `gh pr comment`, because the PR watch prints an unmarked
comment back as if a human wrote it. This text is read by a model, so it
sits in its own commit (`38e4da0`) for the Owner to read alone.
- **Docs and the lists that track scripts:** the header of `pr-watch.ts`
and `AGENTS.md` now name `comment.ts` next to `thread.ts`. `knip.jsonc`
lists it as an entry, and `scripts/lint/layers.map.ts` places it in the
entry layer.
- **Adjacent fix:** `.gitignore` now ignores `node_modules` instead of
`node_modules/`. With the trailing slash, git matched only a directory,
so a worktree whose `node_modules` is a symlink to the main checkout's
showed it as untracked. The Stop hook then refused to publish, because
the tree was not clean.

Closes #87

## How I verified it

- `scripts/land-loop/comment.test.ts`:
- `post` runs `gh pr comment <pr> --body "<comment>\n\n<AUTHOR_MARK>"`.
  - A failed post throws.
  - `argsOf` refuses a missing, blank or non-integer argument.
- One test takes the body `post` actually sends and feeds it to
`wakesOf` as a comment by `bengous`, next to an unmarked comment by
`bengous`. Only the unmarked one prints a Wake.
- `scripts/land-loop/stop/decide.test.ts`: `armReason` contains the
`comment.ts` command with its PR number and the "never with `gh pr
comment`" line.
- `bun check` passes (468 tests).
- `bun scripts/ci/mutation.ts run` on `stop/decide.ts`: no mutant
survives on the changed lines.
- `bun scripts/land-loop/comment.ts` with no arguments prints the usage
error.

test(land-loop): check the commands the Stop hook gives the Author

Closes #87

test(land-loop): state the factory's safety guarantees in a file only the Owner lands (#86)

Since #83, the factory's own code lands without the Owner, including the
code that enforces the Owner's paths and veto. This PR writes the Land
loop's safety guarantees as property tests in one file,
`scripts/land-loop/guarantees.test.ts`. A change to the Routing rules or
to the Merge bot's decision that breaks one of them fails `bun check`
and CI.

**Not routed to the Owner.** The file is a `factoryPaths` path, so a
change to it gets the deep Code review and needs no `land-ok`. This
follows the Owner's principle: a harness, not a prison. The guarantees
are there to catch mistakes, not to add a wait on the Owner. Routing the
file to the Owner would only stop an agent weakening it on purpose, and
the Owner already declined that guard for `bunfig.toml`, `package.json`
and the test preload. This PR no longer touches
`.github/software-factory.json` or `AGENTS.md`.

## The guarantees

Routing rules:

| # | Guarantee | Test |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | A change that touches an `ownerPaths` path or the factory config
never lands auto, whatever the Routing judge answers | "under the lab's
config, a change that touches an ownerPaths path or the factory config
never lands auto, whatever the Routing judge answers" |
| 2 | The factory config goes to the Owner under any routing policy |
"under any routing policy, a change that touches the factory config
never lands auto, whatever the Routing judge answers" |
| 3 | A `factoryPaths` or `deepReviewPaths` change always gets a deep
review | "under the lab's config, a change that touches a factoryPaths
or deepReviewPaths path gets a deep review, whatever the Routing judge
answers" |
| 4 | The config's parser reads the routing policy as the file holds it
| "the routing policy reads as written: the config's parser drops, adds
or changes no glob" |

Merge bot (`decide`):

| # | Guarantee | Test |
|---|---|---|
| 5 | The veto: a PR held by `land:human` or an owner route merges only
with the Owner's Land approval for its patch | "a PR the Owner holds, by
land:human or an owner Routing answer, merges only with the Owner's Land
approval for this very patch" |
| 6 | A Patch delta that a third Review round would read goes to the
Owner | "a Patch delta a third Review round would read merges only with
the Owner's Land approval for this very patch" |
| 7 | No merge on a draft, red or pending CI, an open Important, a
conflict, a red `dev` or an Ejection | "an auto-merge comes last, after
a green Land gate, on a PR that is ready, green, unblocked and routed" |
| 8 | A requested review with no report blocks the merge | "nothing
merges while the review asked for this patch has no report" |
| 9 | A change whose depth is not `none` merges only after a Review
round read it | "a change whose Review depth is not none merges only
once a Review round read it" |
| 10 | A Patch delta its Routing answer asks to read again merges only
after Review round 2 | "a Patch delta its Routing answer asks to read
again never merges before Review round 2 read it" |

## Changes

- `scripts/land-loop/guarantees.test.ts` (new). It holds the guarantees
and the generators they draw from. `pathsOf` turns the config's globs
into path generators. It accepts three forms (`dir/**`, a literal path,
one `*` in a file name) and throws on any other form, so a new glob in
the config fails loudly instead of being skipped.
- A second "near-landable" snapshot generator. The old one almost never
reached a merge (about 14 in 20,000 draws), so its invariants missed
several breakages. In the new one each blocker is absent six times in
seven, which gives about 10% merges. Each Merge bot guarantee runs over
both generators, 2,000 runs each.
- `merge-bot/decide.test.ts` and `routing/routing-rules.test.ts`: the
invariants that stated a guarantee moved into the new file. Both files
import the shared generators from it, and bun then runs the guarantees
inside each of them (checked on bun 1.4.4), so each module's mutation
pass still runs the guarantees.

## Verification

- Each of 19 deliberate breakages, applied alone and then reverted,
turned at least one guarantee red, in repeated runs with random seeds
and under the CI seed `20261106`:
- in `routing-rules.ts`: the config path or `ownerPaths` dropped from
the owner match; the judge's answer overriding a ruled or mixed change;
review depth `light` on owner or factory answers;
  - in `factory-config.ts`: the parser dropping `.github/**`;
- in `decide.ts`: `risen` ignoring `land:human`; the approval ignoring
the patch or who put the label; no hold on red or pending CI, on a draft
or on open Importants; a running or failed review not blocking; no
Review round 1; no Review round 2; a third round not raising to the
Owner.
- `bun check`: green, 464 tests with 0 failures.
- `bun scripts/ci/mutation.ts run`: `decide.ts` 423 mutants,
`routing-rules.ts` 113, 0 undetected on the changed lines and 0 killed
at the base now undetected.

test(land-loop): leave the guarantees file out of ownerPaths, and guarantee Review round 2

The Owner's harness, not a prison: the guarantees catch a change to the Routing
rules or the Merge bot that breaks a promise, and that needs no wait on the
Owner. Routing the file to the Owner only guarded against an agent weakening it
on purpose, a guard the Owner already declined for bunfig.toml, package.json and
the test preload. The file leaves ownerPaths, with its routing test, its pinned
Owner globs and its AGENTS.md mention; a change to it is a factoryPaths change
and gets the deep Code review.

From the review's Nits:
- a Patch delta its Routing answer asks to read again never merges before Review
  round 2 read it: a new guarantee, which a decide that skips round 2 turns red;
- the parser test compares the routing policy only, so a config section the
  parser does not read yet no longer fails it;
- the Routing properties go back to fast-check's default runs, which catch every
  deliberate Routing breakage, and the RUNS comment no longer promises more.

test(land-loop): pin the Owner's paths and the config parser in the guarantees, and set their runs

A change to factory-config.ts, which lands without the Owner, could make the
parser drop a glob from ownerPaths: the ownerPaths guarantee drew only from the
parsed policy, so it would still pass. The guarantee now also draws from the
Owner's globs pinned as literals, and a test checks that the parser reads the
config exactly as the file holds it.

The Routing guarantees pass RUNS, so a global fast-check setting in the test
preload cannot lower how hard they search. The header states that the files
that decide whether this file runs land without the Owner.

build: ignore .claude/settings.local.json in the repository (#85)

`bun check` failed at every stop on `.claude/settings.local.json`, a
per-user file the repository does not own. This PR adds it to the
repository's `.gitignore`.

## Why the file slipped through

- Claude Code rewrites `.claude/settings.local.json` itself each time a
permission is granted. That write is not an Edit or Write tool call, so
the PostToolUse format hook (`scripts/hooks/fix-edited.ts`) never runs
on it.
- The format hook would skip it anyway: it formats only files `git
check-ignore` does not ignore, and the Owner's global git ignore lists
this file.
- `bun fmt --check .` honours the repository's `.gitignore`, not a
global git ignore, so it still read the file and failed.

## Verification

- On a scratch repository: with the file unformatted, `bun fmt --check
.` fails; with the line in the repository's `.gitignore`, it passes.
- `bun fmt --check .` here: all 113 files formatted.

build: ignore .claude/settings.local.json in the repository

Claude Code rewrites this per-user file each time a permission is granted,
outside any Edit or Write call, so the format hook never sees it, and
bun fmt --check . read it: bun fmt honours the repository's .gitignore,
not a global git ignore. Each stop then failed on a file the repository
does not own. Ignoring it here takes it out of the format check.

test(land-loop): state the factory's safety guarantees in a file only the Owner lands

The code that enforces the Land loop's rules lives under scripts/, which lands
without the Owner, so an agent PR could weaken it. scripts/land-loop/guarantees.test.ts
states the guarantees as fast-check properties over routingRulesOf, judgeAskOf,
routingOf and decide, and joins ownerPaths in .github/software-factory.json, so a
change to it needs the Owner's land-ok:

- under the lab's config, an ownerPaths path or the factory config never lands
  auto, whatever the Routing judge answers;
- under any routing policy, the factory config never lands auto;
- a factoryPaths or deepReviewPaths path always gets a deep review;
- a PR held by land:human or an owner Routing answer, or one a third Review round
  would read, merges only on the Owner's Land approval for its patch;
- no auto-merge on a draft, a red or pending CI, an open Important, a conflict,
  a red dev or an Ejection, nor while the review asked for the patch has no
  report, nor before any Review round read a change whose depth is not none.

The config globs become path generators that throw on a glob form they do not
know. The snapshot arbitraries move into the file, so no other file can narrow
what the guarantees draw from, plus a near-landable one under which an auto-merge
is common. The invariants of decide.test.ts and routing-rules.test.ts that stated
the same guarantees move here; both files import the arbitraries from it, so each
module's mutation pass still runs the guarantees.

feat(routing): land the factory's own code without the Owner, from a factory config (#83)

The factory's own code now lands without the Owner's `land-ok`. The
Routing rules read their policy from a new factory config,
`.github/software-factory.json`, and the Land gate waits for `mutation`
as well as `validate`.

**This PR needs the Owner's `land-ok` one last time.** The Merge bot
routes it with the rules already on `dev`, and those send `scripts/`,
`AGENTS.md` and `.github/` to the Owner.

## Routing after this PR

| A PR that touches | Land route | Review |
|---|---|---|
| any `ownerPaths` path, or `.github/software-factory.json` | Owner
(`land-ok`) | deep |
| only `factoryPaths` | auto, once `validate` and `mutation` are green
and no Important is open; any size, breaking or not | deep |
| `factoryPaths` or `deepReviewPaths`, and any path outside
`factoryPaths` | Owner on a breaking commit or past 400 lines; else auto
as above, unless the Routing judge, asked about the paths no rule names,
answers `owner` | deep |
| paths no rule names only (`app/` outside `app/src/store/`, `docs/`,
...) | Owner on a breaking commit or past 400 lines; else the Routing
judge decides | the Routing judge's |

- `ownerPaths`: `.github/**`, `bun.lock`, `scripts/vendor/**`.
`REVIEW.md` puts the last two out of the Code review's scope, so no
review would read them.
- `factoryPaths`: `scripts/**`, `.claude/**` (`settings.json` included),
`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `REVIEW.md`, `package.json`, `mise.toml`,
`tsconfig.json`, `bunfig.toml`, `oxlint*.config.ts`, `.oxfmtrc*`,
`stryker.config.ts`, `knip.json*`, `.mcp.json`.
- `deepReviewPaths`: `app/src/store/**`. It is app code, so it stays
under the cap and the breaking-commit hold.

## Exactly what still reaches the Owner

1. A PR that touches `.github/**`, `bun.lock` or `scripts/vendor/**`.
The factory config itself always goes to the Owner, even when a config
drops it from `ownerPaths`: the rule is in the code. A rename counts
under both its paths, so moving a file out of `.github/` still goes to
the Owner.
2. A PR that touches a path outside `factoryPaths` (`app/src/store/`
included) and has a breaking commit (`type!:` or `BREAKING CHANGE`) or
more than 400 changed lines.
3. A PR that touches a path no rule names, which the Routing judge
(Haiku) routes `owner`, or for which it fails, even when the PR also
touches `factoryPaths`.
4. A PR with no changed file.
5. A PR that would need a third Review round: after Review round 2, a
new risky push gets `needs-human`. Every push to a ruled path counts as
risky, as before.

## The veto

Put `land:human` on any PR. Labels only rise (`risen` in
`merge-bot/decide.ts`), so the route becomes `owner` whatever the rules
said: the Land gate turns pending, "waiting for the Owner's Land
approval", and the PR lands only on `land-ok` for its patch. The veto
holds until the merge queue has re-posted the checks on its own commit
(`queue/repost.ts`); a PR already past that point lands. Converting the
PR to draft or closing it also stops it.

## What changed

The native review of #81, round 2 (run
[42371270575](https://github.com/bengous-labs/software-factory-lab/actions/runs/42371270575),
opus/high), reported three Important findings on the last commits of

| Finding | Change |
|---|---|
| A review run cancelled with no result is dispatched again at once,
with no cap: a review that keeps hitting the job's timeout, or that the
Owner cancels, loops, one paid run each time | `code-review.yml` sets
`cancel-in-progress: false`: a second dispatch waits for the run in
progress, so the review job never cancels one of its runs. `decide.ts`
treats a cancelled run as a failure again. A run GitHub answers 404 for
is its own `ReviewJob` kind, `missing`, and is asked again |
| The adapter's read of the review run had no test |
`reviewJobReader(runner)` takes the runner; tests cover no read for
another patch, 404 as `missing`, any other failure thrown, a run in
progress, and the artifact named `review-<pr>-<round>` |
| The post's unquoted-path diff had no test | `diffArgsOf` holds the
post's git arguments, `core.quotePath=false` included; a test pins them
and reads a non-ASCII path |

```
before (#81)                                 after
Sweep dispatches A, event dispatches B       Sweep dispatches A, event dispatches B
B cancels A (cancel-in-progress: true)       B waits for A (cancel-in-progress: false)
record keeps A -> A asked again, forever     both finish, the record reads its own run

```

The Owner chose this over capping the retries: a cancelled run is a
failure, as D9 says, and the race that the retry answered no longer
exists once the job stops cancelling its own runs. The cost: a review
that a new push made stale runs to its end, and the next review waits
for it (one to two minutes in the runs so far).

repository.

`Bash`, next to the `Stop` and `PostToolUse` hooks.

- its measure differs from the recorded one;
- a function the list does not name breaks a rule its file is excepted
